# fn-159 Convergence-aware review terminals and per-surface blocking calibration

## Goal & Context
<!-- scope: business -->

The deterministic review cap (fn-90/fn-131) counts dispatches, and a dispatch counter cannot distinguish a genuinely stuck review loop from one converging in severity while each fix surfaces one more small finding. Field evidence, 2026-08-02 session (flow-next repo): three plan reviews hit the cap at 4 with only trivial residue left — fn-155 (findings 8→7→3→3, then human reset → SHIP on the next round, having burned 4 rounds at an identical head SHA), fn-153 (severity P0→P1→P2, reset → SHIP), fn-156 (4 findings → 1 stale-prose finding, capped). Meanwhile flow-swarm shows the opposite tail: fn-147 hit the cap on 3 of 4 tasks, round 3's fix introduced a fresh P0, and when the budget ran out six findings were applied by the conductor and shipped **with no re-review** (`SHIP_WITH_CONDUCTOR_FIXES`) — cap exhaustion produced an unreviewed ship, which is worse than an early escalation.

The interim mitigation (already in tree, uncommitted): `MAX_REVIEW_ITERATIONS` default raised 4→8. The docstring names this spec's work as the real fix: a convergence-aware terminal built from the structured findings the system already persists (fn-136), plus an explicit escalate-to-human path, plus per-surface blocking calibration so trivial plan-prose residue stops consuming rounds at all.

The system already produces the convergence signal on every round — per-finding severity, confidence, classification (introduced/pre_existing), status (fixed/not_fixed/withdrawn), and cross-round lineage via `priorFindingId`/`supersedesReceiptId`, schema-validated in receipts — and then ignores it: the cap logic never reads it, and the ratchet's memory is a raw prose blob truncated at 8000 chars.

Second calibration problem: one severity vocabulary and blocking contract is applied to three surfaces doing different jobs. Plan review blocks on prose self-consistency that cannot cause a bad downstream outcome; impl review can re-litigate settled plan decisions; the land-loop PR bot (a black box we cannot re-prompt) gets zero scope guidance in its trigger comment and its prose findings can gate a merge that impl review already passed.

## Architecture & Data Models
<!-- scope: technical -->

All flowctl changes are zero-judgment plumbing (hash comparison, JSON walks over already-validated receipt data, fixed threshold rules) — consistent with the "flowctl grows only under burden of proof" principle. No new LLM calls anywhere. Every new mechanism can only END a loop earlier (early escalate, forced terminal); nothing can grant, refund, or extend rounds.

**Components touched:**

1. **Dispatch guard (flowctl)** — in `enforce_and_increment_review_cap()` (flowctl.py:9429; new code after the sidecar-exists check ~:9460, before the cap branch): before reserving a round, compare a content hash of the reviewed artifact against the hash recorded at the last consumed verdict for the same counter scope. Plan/completion reviews hash the spec markdown body **plus all child task markdown files** (over-inclusion accepted: an unrelated task edit merely permits a dispatch the cap still bounds; under-inclusion would refuse legitimate re-reviews); impl reviews hash the diff content. Reuse `_file_sha256` (:10388) / the normalized-blob hash pattern. Unchanged hash → refuse with `NOT_RETRYABLE: artifact unchanged since last verdict` under the generic error path (exit 1), consuming nothing. `--force` dispatches and consumes normally and stamps `forced: true` on the attempt row. **Hash-compute failure fails OPEN** (dispatch proceeds with a logged warning) — the guard is a waste-saver, never a review-blocker. **Both reset verbs (`spec reset-review-rounds`, `review-rounds reset`) clear the hash baseline together with the counter** — same clean-slate operation, preserving the fn-155 recovery path (reset → re-review without an edit) without `--force`. `review_attempts` rows gain additive `artifact_sha256` (and optional `forced`) at the single row-build site (:9359-9376).
2. **Stall detector (flowctl)** — same call site, after the hash guard: walk the receipt findings lineage (current receipt + archived generations via `load_review_receipt_generations` :6176, bounded to the most recent 6 generations) for the counter scope and exit `REVIEW_CAP_EXIT_CODE` (4) with the existing `ESCALATE:` marker plus a stall sub-reason when any deterministic rule fires. Rules (evaluated only when the last 2 **consecutive consumed verdict rounds in the same counter scope** — regardless of backend or session; the receipt path is shared across backends — both carry valid schemaVersion-1 findings; absent, legacy, or **malformed-but-tagged** containers make the detector inert via `_review_findings_container_valid` :5322 — never a false stall):
   - **Persistent not-fixed:** the same finding `id`/`priorFindingId` chain carries `status: not_fixed` across those 2 rounds.
   - **Flat trajectory:** max open severity did not strictly decrease AND open-finding count did not strictly decrease.
   - **Regressing fixes:** a new `classification: introduced` finding at ≥P1 appears in each of the 2 rounds.
   A `--force`d round is a normal detector input. Lineage lost to `/tmp` cleanup or a host switch → detector inert, cap-only behavior (documented, acceptable).
3. **NEEDS_HUMAN verdict** — added to the verdict grammar as a fourth terminal (`SHIP | NEEDS_WORK | MAJOR_RETHINK | NEEDS_HUMAN`; completion review gains it as a third: `SHIP | NEEDS_WORK | NEEDS_HUMAN`). Parsed by the existing last-`<verdict>`-tag rule (parse regex :4516 — the sanctioned edge; no new parse surface). A delivered NEEDS_HUMAN consumes its round, is recorded on the receipt and `review_attempts`, **writes status `needs_human` in BOTH duplicated status maps** (:9388-9392 and :35838), and the review command exits 4 with `ESCALATE: reviewer requested human review`, so pilot/land/Ralph route it through existing ESCALATE→NEEDS_HUMAN handling. **Four code sites total, not two:** the flowctl maps plus `scripts/hooks/ralph-guard.py` `VALID_RECEIPT_VERDICTS` (L112) and its three `<verdict>(...)` regexes (~L917/932/994) — missing the guard sites makes Ralph reject a legitimate NEEDS_HUMAN receipt. Grammar text updates sweep the four prompt templates + byte-parity fallbacks, skill prose (canonical + codex mirror via sync), ralph-init templates (`ralph.sh`, `prompt_{plan,work,completion}.md`), and GLOSSARY/docs. Standalone (no-sidecar) reviews parse it too; with no driver watching, the exit-4 marker is the interactive user's signal — fine. Prompt guidance (all surfaces): emit NEEDS_HUMAN when the remaining disagreement is a design judgment call — never as a soft NEEDS_WORK.
4. **Ratchet reads structured findings** — `build_convergence_ratchet_block()` (:9598) consumes `findings.items` from the prior receipt (via a structured sibling of `_read_prior_findings` :9547) and renders a compact numbered list (ordinal, severity, classification, status, title, file:line — capped item count so the cursor argv-budget fitter (:36218-36225) never mid-item-truncates; the item-by-item accounting contract applies to rendered items). Prose-blob path retained as a labeled legacy fallback. Injection-neutralization (:9621-9626) and data-not-instructions guards keep current semantics. Applies to all backends incl. host (shared receipt path).
5. **Per-surface calibration (prompt templates + fallbacks; hash-pinned)** —
   - **Plan review** (`references/plan-review-prompt.md`, severity line L65): outcome-anchored severity definitions (P0 = following the plan produces a wrong or impossible implementation; P1 = material ambiguity likely to mislead a competent implementer; P2/P3 = consistency/polish — never blocking). Add the confidence-suppression gate plan review currently lacks (drop <75, P0 exempt at 50+ — parity with impl/completion; suppression applies BEFORE the ratchet contract evaluates blockers). Blocking findings must name the concrete bad downstream outcome they prevent; ratchet rule 2 for plan-kind reviews tightens to require it (test: "could a competent implementer following this plan produce the wrong artifact?").
   - **Impl review** (`references/impl-review-prompt.md`): a "plan is settled" clause — findings re-litigating a decision recorded in the spec's `## Decision Context` (or `knowledge/decisions/`) are FYI, never blocking (mirror pr-comment-resolver.md ~L63-70 wording).
   - **Completion review** (`references/completion-review-prompt.md`): inherits the plan-surface severity definitions (same prose-residue exposure).
6. **Bot-surface bounding (docs + skill prose; the bot itself is a black box)** —
   - `land.reviewTrigger` docs (flowctl.md config table ~L803 + land workflow.md §2.6) gain a recommended trigger text scoping the pass (integration effects, the assembled diff as a narrative, regressions per-task reviews structurally could not see; spec/doc-prose findings welcome as FYI, not merge-gating). Config default stays `""`. The bot's comments deliberately do NOT participate in the stall detector's lineage or any flowctl guard — separate channel, out of blast radius.
   - resolve-pr triage (workflow.md + pr-comment-resolver.md "Decide verdict" table): on a code PR, a spec/doc-prose finding is fix-or-record (spec-touchup commit or reasoned FYI reply + resolve), never merge-gating; a prose finding revealing the code does the wrong thing is a code finding and blocks normally. The resolver's reply names the class it assigned.
7. **Reset-verb + force guarding** — `review-rounds reset`, `spec reset-review-rounds`, **and `--force` on review dispatch/increment** added to the Ralph guard blocklist (`ralph-guard.py` `handle_pre_tool_use` :673, following the existing `re.search`/`output_block` pattern; heed memory lesson `shell-command-allowlist-gates-must-2026-06-05` — tokenize, don't substring-match). All three are human-only; pilot/land/work/ralph prose states it.

**Data flow:** reviewer emits per-finding structured data (existing fn-136 path) → receipt persists it (existing) → flowctl reads it at the next dispatch for guard/detector decisions (new) → drivers see only the existing exit codes and markers.

## API Contracts

- Unchanged-artifact refusal: exit 1 (generic error path) with the literal marker `NOT_RETRYABLE: artifact unchanged since last verdict` so drivers do not loop; no reservation made, no ledger row written. `--force` flag on the increment/dispatch surface overrides (human-only by guard policy).
- `review_attempts` row: additive optional `artifact_sha256` (string), `forced` (bool, present only when true). No schema break; existing readers ignore them.
- Verdict grammar: `NEEDS_HUMAN` accepted on all backends + host; status maps write `needs_human`; receipts record the verdict verbatim. Exit codes 2/3/4/5 unchanged in meaning; 4 gains two marker variants (`ESCALATE: review loop stalled (<rule>)`, `ESCALATE: reviewer requested human review`) alongside the cap marker.
- No `.flow/config.json` key additions or renames (no schema regen needed).

## Edge Cases & Constraints

- **Hard constraints preserved (load-bearing, from fn-90/fn-131 history):** (1) the implementing agent can never reset or extend its own gate — all new mechanisms are shorten-only; reset verbs AND `--force` are guard-blocked; (2) a delivered verdict is never re-framed as a transport failure; (3) the cap can never be disabled or set to zero; (4) every round is a real dispatch with real cost — the stall detector claws back the doubled worst case of the 4→8 raise; (5) exit codes 2/3/4/5 keep their meanings for autonomous drivers.
- **Runaway proof:** worst case remains exactly `MAX_REVIEW_ITERATIONS` real dispatches. Detector and NEEDS_HUMAN only terminate earlier. Transport refunds (fn-131) unchanged; `reset_review_cap` still never touches `review_pending_rounds` (fn-134.7/R22 invariant).
- **Reviewer gaming:** the reviewer could skew severities/statuses to keep rounds alive, but it has no self-grant path — it emits data; flowctl applies fixed rules; extension is bounded by the hard cap regardless. Cross-model, auditable in receipts.
- **Detector false positives:** rules require 2 consecutive qualifying verdict rounds; early escalation on a loop that would have self-resolved at round 5 is acceptable (human sees converged-except-residue and resets). Fail-inert everywhere: legacy/absent/malformed findings, lost lineage, or a hash-compute failure never produce a false stall or a blocked review.
- **NEEDS_HUMAN vs MAJOR_RETHINK:** MAJOR_RETHINK stays "the approach is wrong — redesign"; NEEDS_HUMAN is "a human must adjudicate." Prompts state the distinction so NEEDS_HUMAN doesn't cannibalize either verdict.
- **Prompt-text discipline:** every prompt change updates the SHA-256 pins in `test_prompt_text_pinned.py` in the same commit with rationale; the four extracted-prompt `*_FALLBACK` constants stay byte-identical to templates (`test_review_prompt_template_parity`); `VALIDATOR_TEMPLATE_FALLBACK`/`DEEP_PASSES_FALLBACK` are deliberate condensations — never sync.
- **Cross-platform:** `./scripts/sync-codex.sh` twice (idempotency); canonical prose stays portable; flowctl propagation to `.flow/bin/` + tracker manifest + parity tests per CLAUDE.md final-gate rules. Guard hooks don't fire on Cursor (different hook events) — the reset/force block degrades to prose-only there, as all guard rules already do.
- **Open-spec coordination:** fn-142 (maintainability block, same plan-review prompt) and fn-149 (same land docs) land AFTER fn-159 or rebase onto it — fn-159 owns the severity/contract rewrite; fn-142's block composes on top. fn-120 (flowctl.py Windows sweep) must not run concurrently with fn-159's flowctl edits.
- **No-sidecar reviews stay uncapped** (existing early-return :9460-9462); guard/detector inert without a sidecar.

## Acceptance Criteria
<!-- scope: both -->

- **R1:** flowctl refuses to dispatch a re-review when the reviewed artifact's content hash (plan/completion: spec md + all child task md; impl: diff content) equals the hash at the last consumed verdict for the same counter scope; the refusal consumes no round and prints `NOT_RETRYABLE: artifact unchanged since last verdict` (exit 1). `--force` overrides, consuming normally and stamping `forced: true`. Hash-compute failure fails open with a warning. Both reset verbs clear the hash baseline together with the counter (fn-155 recovery path: reset → re-review with no edit dispatches WITHOUT `--force`). `review_attempts` rows record `artifact_sha256`.
- **R2:** flowctl exits 4 with `ESCALATE: review loop stalled (<rule>)` when, over the last 2 consecutive consumed verdict rounds in the same counter scope (backend/session-independent), both rounds carry valid schemaVersion-1 findings and any of: the same finding chain stays `not_fixed`; max open severity AND open count both fail to strictly decrease; a new `introduced` ≥P1 finding appears in each round. Absent, legacy, malformed, or lost findings leave behavior identical to today (never a false stall). Generation walk bounded to the 6 most recent.
- **R3:** `NEEDS_HUMAN` is a parseable terminal verdict on all four backends and the host path; it consumes its round, lands on the receipt, writes status `needs_human` in BOTH flowctl status maps (:9388, :35838), passes `ralph-guard.py` (`VALID_RECEIPT_VERDICTS` + all three verdict regexes updated), and the review command exits 4 with `ESCALATE: reviewer requested human review`. pilot, land, and Ralph route it via existing ESCALATE handling with no driver logic changes.
- **R4:** the convergence ratchet renders prior findings from structured `findings.items` (numbered; severity/classification/status; item-count-capped for the cursor argv budget) when schemaVersion-1 findings exist, with the prose blob as labeled legacy fallback; injection-neutralization behavior preserved and tested.
- **R5:** the plan-review prompt defines P0–P3 in downstream-outcome terms, carries the confidence-suppression gate (drop <75, P0 exempt at 50+; suppression precedes the ratchet contract), and requires blocking findings to name the concrete bad outcome; plan-kind ratchet rule 2 requires the same. The completion-review prompt inherits the outcome-anchored severity definitions. The fn-156-class finding (true self-contradiction, no downstream consequence) is non-blocking under the new text; the fn-153-class finding (plan makes a task impossible) blocks.
- **R6:** the impl-review prompt states that findings re-litigating a recorded Decision Context decision are FYI, never blocking.
- **R7:** resolve-pr triage classifies spec/doc-prose findings on code PRs as fix-or-record (never merge-gating), with the prose-reveals-behavior-gap carve-out treated as a code finding; the resolver's reply names the class.
- **R8:** land docs (flowctl.md `land.reviewTrigger` row + land workflow §2.6) document a recommended trigger text that scopes the bot pass and declares prose findings FYI; the config default remains `""`; docs state bot comments are outside the detector/guard blast radius.
- **R9:** `review-rounds reset`, `spec reset-review-rounds`, and `--force` on review dispatch/increment are blocked by ralph-guard (tokenized matching, not substring); pilot/land/work/ralph skill prose states all three are human-only.
- **R10:** the 4→8 default raise ships with this spec: the `## Unreleased` CHANGELOG entry covers the raise + rationale AND the detector/NEEDS_HUMAN/ratchet/calibration work, user-outcome-first per releasing.md; all user-facing docs state 8 consistently.
- **R11:** full gate green: focused suites per task; final gate runs `python3 scripts/run_tests_parallel.py` + `uvx ruff@0.16.0 check .`; prompt-hash pins updated with rationale; flowctl propagated to `.flow/bin/` (`flowctl.py` target, never the bash launcher) + tracker manifest regenerated; `sync-codex.sh` run twice with mirror diff committed.
- **R12:** STRATEGY.md's Ralph track quality-discipline sentence is extended to name convergence-aware review terminals (trajectory-based early escalation + reviewer-emitted NEEDS_HUMAN); no other strategy edits.
- **R13:** downstream chain walked in the same workstream per the maintainer's downstream-properties instructions: flow-next.dev pages for review caps/land/orchestration updated, docs-site changelog entry staged, AI×SDLC guide checked for touched pages (explicit "checked, no-op" allowed per page), vault notes (Autonomy / Release Timeline) updated.

## Boundaries
<!-- scope: business -->

- **Do NOT shrink or demote impl review.** flow-swarm evidence: impl review produced P0s on 6 of 9 receipted tasks and catches fix-induced regressions across rounds; the PR bot found zero issues on fully impl-reviewed PRs. Complementary surfaces; only blocking calibration changes.
- **No reviewer-decides-budget designs.** The reviewer emits data and terminal verdicts only; round arithmetic stays in flowctl. No "should this get another round?" question to any model.
- **No new LLM calls, no new subprocess judges.** Guard and detector are pure plumbing.
- **No new exit codes; no changes to 2/3/4/5 semantics.** Drivers must not need logic changes.
- **Completion review keeps sharing the plan counter.** Split is unproven need — out of scope.
- **No-sidecar (standalone) reviews stay uncapped** — separate concern.
- **No flow-swarm repo changes.** The land-bypass/manual-merge hygiene there is operator follow-up.
- **No per-surface rubric rewrites.** The 8 numbered criteria per surface already diverge fully; only severity definitions, gates, and blocking contracts change.
- **The cap stays count-based and enabled.** No trajectory rule may raise, refund, or disable it.
- **No changes to fn-131 transport-refund machinery** or the `review_pending_rounds` reset invariant.

## Strategy Alignment

Active tracks served by this plan:
- **Ralph autonomous mode** — hardens the loop suite's quality-discipline invariant: reviews now stop on measured non-convergence or reviewer escalation instead of only on a burned budget; cap exhaustion can no longer silently produce an unreviewed ship.
- **flow-swarm preparation** — first in-house consumer of the fn-136 structured-findings contract (the stall detector and ratchet read `findings.items` exactly as a downstream product would), proving the receipt boundary on our own machinery.

Design-principle fit: the detector is an unattended-trust rail (the sanctioned deterministic category), not model-weakness scaffolding; all flowctl additions are zero-judgment (burden-of-proof met); everything that weighs or judges (severity, prose-vs-behavior classification) stays with the models.

## Decision Context

Why trajectory-augmented count cap over the alternatives. **Raise-to-8 alone** doubles the worst case on stuck specs and was explicitly labeled interim in the docstring that shipped it. **Replace count with model-judged convergence** violates the load-bearing constraint that the agent can never extend its own gate, and asking the reviewer "another round?" hands it a budget decision it has no business owning. **Refund fix-induced-residue rounds** makes the classifier the loophole that swallows the cap — rejected; residue headroom comes from the raised cap, and trivial residue is instead prevented from blocking at all via the plan-surface outcome test. The chosen design keeps every fn-90/fn-131 property (deterministic counter, transport refunds, distinct exit codes, ESCALATE-not-retry) and adds only shorten-only terminals computed by flowctl from reviewer-emitted structured data — cross-model signal, not self-assessment, and it cannot self-grant because it never touches arithmetic. Gap-analysis decisions folded in: reset clears the hash baseline (reset and baseline are one clean-slate operation — anything else re-breaks the fn-155 recovery the guard was motivated by); `--force` is human-only and guard-blocked (otherwise a retry-with-force habit in an autonomous loop trivially defeats the guard); NEEDS_HUMAN writes a real `needs_human` status (drivers read status fields, not just exit codes — a silent `None` would leave state lying); hash failure fails open while findings-parse failure fails inert (a guard that blocks legitimate reviews on an I/O hiccup is worse than the waste it prevents; a detector that stalls on malformed data manufactures false escalations). Per-surface divergence is deliberately confined to severity definitions and blocking contracts because the evidence showed the rubrics already diverge (0 of 8 numbered criteria shared) and the observed failures were calibration failures: plan reviews blocking on outcome-free prose (fn-155/153/156), impl review lacking a settled-plan clause, and the un-promptable PR bot over-weighted in flow-next (prose findings gating merges) while structurally ignored in flow-swarm (17/23 reviews post-merge). The bot stays a bounded-and-filtered safety net: scope via the trigger comment we control, blocking-ness via resolve-pr triage we control.

## Quick commands

```bash
cd plugins/flow-next/tests && python3 -m unittest test_review_convergence_cap test_host_review_backend test_prompt_text_pinned test_review_prompt_template_parity -q
```

## Early proof point

Task fn-159-convergence-aware-review-terminals-and.1 validates the core approach (a deterministic, shorten-only terminal computed inside `enforce_and_increment_review_cap` from persisted state, refusing/escalating without breaking any existing dispatch path or driver contract). If the hash guard can't be wired there without disturbing the reserve/finalize/refund invariants, re-evaluate the call-site placement before building the stall detector on the same seam.

## Requirement coverage

|-----|-------------|---------|-------------------|
| R1  | Artifact-hash dispatch guard + `--force` + reset-clears-baseline | fn-159-convergence-aware-review-terminals-and.1 | — |
| R2  | Deterministic stall detector on findings lineage | fn-159-convergence-aware-review-terminals-and.2 | — |
| R3  | NEEDS_HUMAN terminal verdict end-to-end (4 code sites + grammar sweep) | fn-159-convergence-aware-review-terminals-and.3 | — |
| R4  | Ratchet renders structured findings.items | fn-159-convergence-aware-review-terminals-and.2 | — |
| R5  | Plan/completion severity + confidence gate + outcome test | fn-159-convergence-aware-review-terminals-and.4 | — |
| R6  | Impl-review settled-plan clause | fn-159-convergence-aware-review-terminals-and.4 | — |
| R7  | resolve-pr prose-non-blocking triage rule | fn-159-convergence-aware-review-terminals-and.5 | — |
| R8  | Recommended land.reviewTrigger scope text in docs | fn-159-convergence-aware-review-terminals-and.5 | — |
| R9  | Guard-block reset verbs + `--force`; human-only prose | fn-159-convergence-aware-review-terminals-and.5 | — |
| R10 | CHANGELOG Unreleased entry (raise + this work) + docs say 8 | fn-159-convergence-aware-review-terminals-and.6 | — |
| R11 | Full gate + propagation + sync + hash pins | fn-159-convergence-aware-review-terminals-and.6 | — |
| R12 | STRATEGY.md Ralph-track sentence | fn-159-convergence-aware-review-terminals-and.6 | — |
| R13 | Downstream chain (flow-next.dev, guide, vault) | fn-159-convergence-aware-review-terminals-and.6 | — |

**Data flow:** reviewer emits per-finding structured data (existing fn-136 path) → receipt persists it (existing) → flowctl reads it at the next dispatch for guard/detector decisions (new) → drivers see only the existing exit codes and markers.

## API Contracts

* Unchanged-artifact refusal: exit 1 (generic error path) with the literal marker `NOT_RETRYABLE: artifact unchanged since last verdict` so drivers do not loop; no reservation made, no ledger row written. `--force` flag on the increment/dispatch surface overrides (human-only by guard policy).
* `review_attempts` row: additive optional `artifact_sha256` (string), `forced` (bool, present only when true). No schema break; existing readers ignore them.
* Verdict grammar: `NEEDS_HUMAN` accepted on all backends + host; status maps write `needs_human`; receipts record the verdict verbatim. Exit codes 2/3/4/5 unchanged in meaning; 4 gains two marker variants (`ESCALATE: review loop stalled (<rule>)`, `ESCALATE: reviewer requested human review`) alongside the cap marker.
* No `.flow/config.json` key additions or renames (no schema regen needed).

## Edge Cases & Constraints

* **Hard constraints preserved (load-bearing, from fn-90/fn-131 history):** (1) the implementing agent can never reset or extend its own gate — all new mechanisms are shorten-only; reset verbs AND `--force` are guard-blocked; (2) a delivered verdict is never re-framed as a transport failure; (3) the cap can never be disabled or set to zero; (4) every round is a real dispatch with real cost — the stall detector claws back the doubled worst case of the 4→8 raise; (5) exit codes 2/3/4/5 keep their meanings for autonomous drivers.
* **Runaway proof:** worst case remains exactly `MAX_REVIEW_ITERATIONS` real dispatches. Detector and NEEDS_HUMAN only terminate earlier. Transport refunds (fn-131) unchanged; `reset_review_cap` still never touches `review_pending_rounds` (fn-134.7/R22 invariant).
* **Reviewer gaming:** the reviewer could skew severities/statuses to keep rounds alive, but it has no self-grant path — it emits data; flowctl applies fixed rules; extension is bounded by the hard cap regardless. Cross-model, auditable in receipts.
* **Detector false positives:** rules require 2 consecutive qualifying verdict rounds; early escalation on a loop that would have self-resolved at round 5 is acceptable (human sees converged-except-residue and resets). Fail-inert everywhere: legacy/absent/malformed findings, lost lineage, or a hash-compute failure never produce a false stall or a blocked review.
* **NEEDS_HUMAN vs MAJOR_RETHINK:** MAJOR_RETHINK stays "the approach is wrong — redesign"; NEEDS_HUMAN is "a human must adjudicate." Prompts state the distinction so NEEDS_HUMAN doesn't cannibalize either verdict.
* **Prompt-text discipline:** every prompt change updates the SHA-256 pins in `test_prompt_text_pinned.py` in the same commit with rationale; the four extracted-prompt `*_FALLBACK` constants stay byte-identical to templates (`test_review_prompt_template_parity`); `VALIDATOR_TEMPLATE_FALLBACK`/`DEEP_PASSES_FALLBACK` are deliberate condensations — never sync.
* **Cross-platform:** `./scripts/sync-codex.sh` twice (idempotency); canonical prose stays portable; flowctl propagation to `.flow/bin/` + tracker manifest + parity tests per CLAUDE.md final-gate rules. Guard hooks don't fire on Cursor (different hook events) — the reset/force block degrades to prose-only there, as all guard rules already do.
* **Open-spec coordination:** fn-142 (maintainability block, same plan-review prompt) and fn-149 (same land docs) land AFTER fn-159 or rebase onto it — fn-159 owns the severity/contract rewrite; fn-142's block composes on top. fn-120 ([flowctl.py](<http://flowctl.py>) Windows sweep) must not run concurrently with fn-159's flowctl edits.
* **No-sidecar reviews stay uncapped** (existing early-return :9460-9462); guard/detector inert without a sidecar.

## Boundaries

<!-- scope: business -->

* **Do NOT shrink or demote impl review.** flow-swarm evidence: impl review produced P0s on 6 of 9 receipted tasks and catches fix-induced regressions across rounds; the PR bot found zero issues on fully impl-reviewed PRs. Complementary surfaces; only blocking calibration changes.
* **No reviewer-decides-budget designs.** The reviewer emits data and terminal verdicts only; round arithmetic stays in flowctl. No "should this get another round?" question to any model.
* **No new LLM calls, no new subprocess judges.** Guard and detector are pure plumbing.
* **No new exit codes; no changes to 2/3/4/5 semantics.** Drivers must not need logic changes.
* **Completion review keeps sharing the plan counter.** Split is unproven need — out of scope.
* **No-sidecar (standalone) reviews stay uncapped** — separate concern.
* **No flow-swarm repo changes.** The land-bypass/manual-merge hygiene there is operator follow-up.
* **No per-surface rubric rewrites.** The 8 numbered criteria per surface already diverge fully; only severity definitions, gates, and blocking contracts change.
* **The cap stays count-based and enabled.** No trajectory rule may raise, refund, or disable it.
* **No changes to fn-131 transport-refund machinery** or the `review_pending_rounds` reset invariant.

## Strategy Alignment

Active tracks served by this plan:

* **Ralph autonomous mode** — hardens the loop suite's quality-discipline invariant: reviews now stop on measured non-convergence or reviewer escalation instead of only on a burned budget; cap exhaustion can no longer silently produce an unreviewed ship.
* **flow-swarm preparation** — first in-house consumer of the fn-136 structured-findings contract (the stall detector and ratchet read `findings.items` exactly as a downstream product would), proving the receipt boundary on our own machinery.

Design-principle fit: the detector is an unattended-trust rail (the sanctioned deterministic category), not model-weakness scaffolding; all flowctl additions are zero-judgment (burden-of-proof met); everything that weighs or judges (severity, prose-vs-behavior classification) stays with the models.

## Decision Context

Why trajectory-augmented count cap over the alternatives. **Raise-to-8 alone** doubles the worst case on stuck specs and was explicitly labeled interim in the docstring that shipped it. **Replace count with model-judged convergence** violates the load-bearing constraint that the agent can never extend its own gate, and asking the reviewer "another round?" hands it a budget decision it has no business owning. **Refund fix-induced-residue rounds** makes the classifier the loophole that swallows the cap — rejected; residue headroom comes from the raised cap, and trivial residue is instead prevented from blocking at all via the plan-surface outcome test. The chosen design keeps every fn-90/fn-131 property (deterministic counter, transport refunds, distinct exit codes, ESCALATE-not-retry) and adds only shorten-only terminals computed by flowctl from reviewer-emitted structured data — cross-model signal, not self-assessment, and it cannot self-grant because it never touches arithmetic. Gap-analysis decisions folded in: reset clears the hash baseline (reset and baseline are one clean-slate operation — anything else re-breaks the fn-155 recovery the guard was motivated by); `--force` is human-only and guard-blocked (otherwise a retry-with-force habit in an autonomous loop trivially defeats the guard); NEEDS_HUMAN writes a real `needs_human` status (drivers read status fields, not just exit codes — a silent `None` would leave state lying); hash failure fails open while findings-parse failure fails inert (a guard that blocks legitimate reviews on an I/O hiccup is worse than the waste it prevents; a detector that stalls on malformed data manufactures false escalations). Per-surface divergence is deliberately confined to severity definitions and blocking contracts because the evidence showed the rubrics already diverge (0 of 8 numbered criteria shared) and the observed failures were calibration failures: plan reviews blocking on outcome-free prose (fn-155/153/156), impl review lacking a settled-plan clause, and the un-promptable PR bot over-weighted in flow-next (prose findings gating merges) while structurally ignored in flow-swarm (17/23 reviews post-merge). The bot stays a bounded-and-filtered safety net: scope via the trigger comment we control, blocking-ness via resolve-pr triage we control.
